session.name: MPI-567 session 8 - the box seam is a DC offset on smooth ground, and one node fixes it

goal.original: Fix the visible box edge before any app wiring, working the four candidates in research/lanpaint/verdict.md cheapest-first.
goal.summary: The seam is FIXED and the app half is unblocked. All four candidates failed, but so did the bar they were judged against: `edge_step` is mean |diff| and cannot tell a tonal STEP from redrawn TEXTURE. Splitting those apart showed the real defect is a DC offset landing on a low-variance region, and one node removes it. The next session rebuilds the graph (it still holds the OLD route) and then does the app half.

completed: ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED. Session 7 guessed VAE round-trip + rescale drift. `edge_profile.py` disproves it: drift has no direction, but the signed diff is large and GROWS with depth into the box (sun right -19 -> -33; overcast +9 -> +14 on every edge). The model re-grades everything the noise mask lets it touch. `norescale` is byte-identical to base, so the rescale half of that guess was a no-op all along.

ALL FOUR CANDIDATES RUN AND DEAD (17 configs, `seamfix.py`, numbers in `seamfix_results.json`). (1) `mask_blend_pixels` caps at 64 - 96/128 do not exist; at 64 the edge is unmoved and `outside` leaks WORSE. (2) `denoise` is quantised away at 4 steps (`int(steps/denoise)` makes 0.85 byte-identical to 1.0) and values that bite take anime's shadow to 8%. (3) `ImageCompositeMasked` vs the original crop is a NO-OP BY CONSTRUCTION - its mask is the box, which is what the stitch already blends with. (4) Splitting crop from denoise mask is the right family but every variant lands on one trade curve.

THE BAR ITSELF WAS WRONG, and this is the session's real finding. `edge_step` is mean |diff|, which sums two things the eye treats differently: a DIRECTIONAL offset (`dir = signed/abs -> +-1`, the band moved as a block = a seam) and TEXTURE CHURN (`dir -> 0`, the model redrew gravel/grass at the same average tone = invisible at any magnitude). Visibility is `cnr = |signed| / std(photo in that band)`. `seamvis.py` computes all of it.

THE NUMBERS THAT PROVE IT: sun's top edge scores `abs` 10.98 and is INVISIBLE (dir 0.10, photo std 51.6, cnr 0.02); overcast's top scores a LOWER 9.26 and is the worst seam in the set (dir 1.00, photo std 10.9, cnr 0.85). Verified by eye at 1:1 in `SHEET_compare_base_s096_top.png`. So the defect was never 'the box edge' - it is a DC offset on a low-variance region, which is why it hit overcast on all three edges, hit sun only where the shadow was clipped, and never really hit anime.

THE FIX IS ONE NODE - `f096`: `GrowMaskWithBlur(expand -96, blur_radius 96)` between `InpaintCropImproved`'s `cropped_mask` (output 2) and `SetLatentNoiseMask`. Session 7's `auto` box (+25% out, +60% down) is UNCHANGED. Worst cnr 0.85 -> 0.15, `far_mean` 0.138/0.157/0.159 vs base 0.154/0.223/0.248 (it moves LESS of the photo than baseline), same 16.1s. Runner-up `s096` (tight +12% core, grown 96, feathered 96) scores cnr 0.18 and has the best-looking sun shadow, but it changes box seeding too, so `f096` is the smaller change.

9B IS NOT THE LEVER. Measured for the first time: base 24.80/10.36/8.71 vs 4B's 30.84/12.82/9.33, and with the feather it lands on 4B's numbers (10.71/6.68/2.79 vs 10.39/6.31/2.48). The seam is a property of the route, not the checkpoint. 9B still wins on quality per session 7.

key_decisions: JUDGE THE SEAM WITH `cnr`, NEVER `edge_step`. `seamvis.py` splits mean |diff| into a directional component and texture churn. An abs threshold ranks configs WRONG in both directions: it called sun's invisible top edge (10.98) a failure, and crowned `g192` at 0.40/1.13/0.86 when `g192` is actually the second-worst seam measured (overcast cnr 0.53) because growing the box moved its top edge into smooth SKY (std 2.64), where a 1.39 DC lift is plainly visible. DO NOT SHIP g192.

JUDGE THE SHADOW WITH `objsheet.py`, NEVER `shadow_ratio`. That ratio counts changed pixels outside the object bbox, so it credits the re-grade as shadow: overcast base scores 1.04 largely because the whole box is a visibly lighter rectangle in the grass. `f096`'s 0.48 is that rectangle REMOVED with a real cast shadow still on the ground in all three plates. The apparent 'shadow loss' of every clean config is mostly re-grade removal.

SEAM VISIBILITY IS SCENE-DEPENDENT, and that is a product fact, not just a measurement one. The same DC offset is invisible in gravel (std 51.6) and glaring in smooth grass or sky (std 10.9 / 2.6). So this defect will hit users on plain backgrounds - skies, still water, plain walls - and effectively never on textured ones. Worth remembering when the box step's copy is written.

ALWAYS assert your own SaveImage prefix produced a file - seamfix.py does.

Windows python also needs sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding='utf-8') or it dies on cp1252 mid-script, and json.load on a board file needs encoding='utf-8-sig'.
